- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward more aggressively.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” buffer to prevent overcorrection.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; add a “reversion bias” term toward historical mean or 30-day moving average.
- If model forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows sudden drop (e.g., >5% in 3–5 days), reduce forecast slope or introduce early warning lag correction.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model often fails to account for sentiment-driven volatility; weight sentiment more heavily in later days (e.g., last 5–7 days) for adjustment.
